record.original_question: Determine whether there is a theoretical upper limit on the design parameter t for which the Assmus-Mattson theorem can produce t-designs from linear codes, or else prove that no such limit exists by exhibiting codes that yield t-designs for arbitrarily large t.

evidence.quote: Open Question 5.2. Find a theoretical limit for t such that there exists t-designs via the Assmus-Mattson theorem applied to a linear code, or prove that no such limit exists by finding codes with t-designs for arbitrary t.

artifact.category_tag: Assmus-Mattson theorem and t-designs from codes
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A linear $[n,k,d]$ code $C$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ is a $k$-dimensional subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, where $d$ denotes its minimum Hamming distance. Its dual code $C^\perp$ is defined with respect to the standard inner product and has minimum distance denoted $d^\perp$. For a codeword $c\in C$, its support is $\mathrm{supp}(c)=\{i:c_i\neq 0\}\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$. For each integer $w$, let $\mathcal{B}_w(C)$ denote the multiset of supports of codewords of $C$ of Hamming weight $w$ (taken up to scalar multiplication). A $t$-$(n,w,\lambda)$ design is a collection of $w$-element blocks from an $n$-element point set such that every $t$-element subset of points lies in exactly $\lambda$ blocks.
        
The Assmus–Mattson theorem asserts: let $C$ be an $[n,k,d]$ linear code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with dual code $C^\perp$ of minimum distance $d^\perp$. Fix a positive integer $t<d$. If the number of nonzero weights in $C^\perp$ that are at most $n-t$ is at most $d-t$, then for every $w$ with $d\le w\le n$, the supports $\mathcal{B}_w(C)$ form (the blocks of) a $t$-design (and similarly for $C^\perp$).

Problem. Either:
(a) prove that there exists an absolute upper bound $T<\infty$ such that, for every prime power $q$, every length $n$, and every linear code $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, the largest value of $t$ for which the Assmus–Mattson theorem applied to $C$ produces a nontrivial $t$-design is at most $T$; or
(b) prove no such bound exists, by exhibiting, for every positive integer $t$, a linear code $C$ over some finite field for which the Assmus–Mattson theorem yields a $t$-design.
artifact.status_search_result: No proof of either a universal upper bound on $t$ or a construction giving arbitrarily large $t$ via the Assmus–Mattson theorem has been located. Recent literature (e.g., results bounding $t\le 5$ for certain four-weight binary codes, and Assmus–Mattson-type theorems extended to association schemes, rank-metric codes, and codes over $\mathbb{Z}_4$) studies specific classes but does not settle the general question, which appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Infinite families of 2-designs and 3-designs from linear codes
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of 2- and 3-designs from linear codes via the Assmus–Mattson theorem; higher-t constructions are not provided.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art constructions via Assmus–Mattson typically yield small t (2 or 3); no general bound or unbounded-t family is established.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Assmus–Mattson theorem for some binary codes II
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work investigates restrictions on t for designs arising from Assmus–Mattson for specific weight-class codes.
status_evidence.claim: The question of a universal limit on t in the Assmus–Mattson theorem continues to receive attention, suggesting it is unresolved in general.
